subproblem.title: The pull-back of a bounded continuous form along a C¹ map, cut off to G, is measurable and bounded by WΛⁿ
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let G, O ⊆ ℝ^P be open with G ⊆ O, let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be of class C¹ on O, let ω : ℝ^P → Covector (Euclid P) n (a DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) be continuous with ‖ω(z)‖ ≤ W for every z (operator norm on n-covectors), and let Λ ≥ 0 with ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ Λ for every x ∈ G (Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x, operator norm). Let φ := 1_G·(x ↦ ω(f(x))∘Df(x)), i.e. φ(x) = (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) for x ∈ G and φ(x) = 0 for x ∉ G. Then φ is a.e.-strongly measurable with respect to every measure μ on ℝ^P, and ‖φ(x)‖ ≤ W·Λⁿ for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (G O : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (Λ W : ℝ), IsOpen G → IsOpen O → G ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → Continuous ω → 0 ≤ Λ → (∀ x ∈ G, ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖ ≤ Λ) → (∀ z, ‖ω z‖ ≤ W) → (∀ μ : Measure (Euclid P), AEStronglyMeasurable (G.indicator fun y => (ω (f y)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f y)) μ) ∧ ∀ x, ‖G.indicator (fun y => (ω (f y)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f y)) x‖ ≤ W * Λ ^ n
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent-supplied proof of the selected node: the form φ = 1_G·ω(f)∘Df is Borel and ‖φ‖ ≤ ‖ω‖_∞Λⁿ. This is the pointwise estimate |ω(f(x))∘df_x| ≤ |ω|·|Df(x)|ⁿ behind Simon's push-forward formula (Ch. 6, 2.24(2)–(3), chapter-06.txt lines 414–440) and mass bound (Ch. 6, 2.29, lines 503–507).
Notation. Cov := Covector (Euclid P) n, the space of n-covectors on ℝ^P (continuous alternating maps), with the operator norm. g(x) := ω(f(x))∘Df(x) = (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) ∈ Cov for x ∈ ℝ^P, so φ = G.indicator g. ‖Df(x)‖ is the operator norm. The letter Λ denotes only the derivative bound.
1. Continuity of Df on O. f is C¹ on the open set O, so x ↦ Df(x) is continuous on O (Mathlib ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen, with 1 ≤ 1).
2. Continuity of ω∘f on O. A C¹ map is continuous, so f is continuous on O (ContDiffOn.continuousOn). ω is continuous, so x ↦ ω(f(x)) is continuous on O (Continuous.comp_continuousOn).
3. Continuity of g on G. For a continuous linear map L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P, let A(L) : Cov → Cov, α ↦ α∘L, be the pull-back. It is a continuous linear map (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM, with A(L)(α) = α.compContinuousLinearMap L). The map L ↦ A(L) is continuous (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM; the index type Fin n is finite). Evaluation (A, α) ↦ A(α) of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous. Hence g(x) = A(Df(x))(ω(f(x))) is continuous on O by steps 1–2 (ContinuousOn.clm_apply), in particular on G ⊆ O.
4. Measurability for every measure μ on ℝ^P. G is open, hence a Borel (measurable) set. A function that is continuous on a measurable set s is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞s, since ℝ^P is second countable and Cov is a metric space (Mathlib ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable). So g is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞G. As G is measurable, this is equivalent to a.e.-strong measurability of φ = G.indicator g for μ (Mathlib aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff). This is the first conclusion.
5. W ≥ 0, because 0 ≤ ‖ω(0)‖ ≤ W.
6. Bound on G. Let x ∈ G, so φ(x) = g(x). The operator-norm estimate for pull-backs of alternating maps (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le: ‖α∘L‖ ≤ ‖α‖·‖L‖^{#Fin n}, with #Fin n = n) gives
‖φ(x)‖ ≤ ‖ω(f(x))‖·‖Df(x)‖ⁿ ≤ W·Λⁿ.
The last inequality multiplies 0 ≤ ‖ω(f(x))‖ ≤ W by 0 ≤ ‖Df(x)‖ⁿ ≤ Λⁿ, using W ≥ 0 (step 5). The bound ‖Df(x)‖ⁿ ≤ Λⁿ follows from 0 ≤ ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ Λ, since t ↦ tⁿ is monotone on [0, ∞).
7. Bound off G. Let x ∉ G. Then φ(x) = 0, so ‖φ(x)‖ = 0 ≤ W·Λⁿ, because W ≥ 0 (step 5) and Λ ≥ 0 (hypothesis) give Λⁿ ≥ 0.
Steps 6–7 give ‖φ(x)‖ ≤ W·Λⁿ for every x, the second conclusion. ∎

Lean implementation notes (context, not part of the numbered proof). The script below was checked with `lake env lean` after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission` in namespace GMT.Ch07 with the contract's opens, as the body of `theorem Submission.dor_lmb_pc_cm_pullback_field_bounded : <frozen type> := by`; no sibling is used. #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
```lean
  intro P n G O f ω Λ W hG hO hGO hf hω hΛ hDf hW
  have hcont : ContinuousOn
      (fun y => (ω (f y)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f y)) G := by
    have h1 : ContinuousOn (fun y => fderiv ℝ f y) O := hf.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen hO le_rfl
    have h2 : ContinuousOn (fun y => ω (f y)) O := hω.comp_continuousOn hf.continuousOn
    have h3 : ContinuousOn (fun y => ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM
        (fderiv ℝ f y) (ω (f y))) O :=
      (ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM.comp_continuousOn h1).clm_apply h2
    exact h3.mono hGO
  have hW0 : 0 ≤ W := (norm_nonneg _).trans (hW 0)
  refine ⟨fun μ => ?_, fun x => ?_⟩
  · rw [aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff hG.measurableSet]
    exact hcont.aestronglyMeasurable hG.measurableSet
  · by_cases hx : x ∈ G
    · rw [Set.indicator_of_mem hx]
      calc ‖(ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)‖
          ≤ ‖ω (f x)‖ * ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖ ^ Fintype.card (Fin n) :=
            ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le _ _
        _ = ‖ω (f x)‖ * ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖ ^ n := by rw [Fintype.card_fin]
        _ ≤ W * Λ ^ n := mul_le_mul (hW _) (pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) (hDf x hx) n)
            (pow_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) _) hW0
    · rw [Set.indicator_of_notMem hx, norm_zero]
      exact mul_nonneg hW0 (pow_nonneg hΛ n)
```
proof_key_steps: Df is continuous on O (f ∈ C¹(O)), and so is ω∘f.
L ↦ (α ↦ α∘L) is continuous (compContinuousLinearMapCLM), so g = ω(f)∘Df is continuous on G ⊆ O.
Continuity on the open, hence measurable, set G gives a.e.-strong measurability of 1_G·g for every measure.
‖α∘L‖ ≤ ‖α‖‖L‖ⁿ gives ‖φ‖ ≤ WΛⁿ on G; off G, φ = 0 and WΛⁿ ≥ 0.

audit.reason: The proof establishes derivative continuity on open O, pullback continuity on G, and indicator measurability for every measure using the applicable second-countability instance. It derives W ≥ 0 and proves the stated bound both on and off G. No continuity on closure G or finite-measure hypothesis is needed.
